It works Monday. Tuesday it hallucinates, makes up a company policy, and tells a customer something completely wrong. Your only debugging option is reading raw JSON logs. \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay\u003c/code\u003e records every step of every agent run — every thought, tool call, retrieval, and output — so you can replay exactly what happened, step by step, like rewinding a tape.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2. \"It worked before, what changed?\"\u003c/strong\u003e\nYou push a new prompt or swap a model and suddenly your agent breaks on cases that used to work. \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay diff\u003c/code\u003e puts two runs side-by-side and shows you exactly where they diverged — which step went different, what changed in the context, where things went wrong.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. \"How do I test a fix without rerunning everything?\"\u003c/strong\u003e\nYou think you know what went wrong but you don't want to burn API credits and time reproducing the exact scenario. \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay fork\u003c/code\u003e lets you take any recorded run, rewind to any step, change the input, and see what would have happened differently.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e4. \"How do I know if my agent is actually good?\"\u003c/strong\u003e\nYou have no systematic way to evaluate agent quality. \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay eval\u003c/code\u003e runs automatic checks — hallucination detection, safety audits, completeness checks — using both deterministic rules and AI-powered analysis. Bring your own API key (Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI) and get root-cause analysis, quality scoring, security audits, and optimization suggestions for pennies per trace.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e5. \"How do I stop my agent from doing dangerous things?\"\u003c/strong\u003e\nYour agent has access to tools that can delete data, send emails, or make purchases. \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay guard\u003c/code\u003e lets you define kill-switch policies that flag or block dangerous patterns — like blocking any \u003ccode\u003edelete\u003c/code\u003e tool calls, or warning when token usage spikes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e6. \"How do I build regression tests for a non-deterministic system?\"\u003c/strong\u003e\nEvery time you To capture a run \u003cstrong\u003eas it happens\u003c/strong\u003e, stream newline-delimited capture events into \u003ccode\u003erecord\u003c/code\u003e — the trace grows step by step and stays \u003ccode\u003erunning\u003c/code\u003e until a \u003ccode\u003etrace_end\u003c/code\u003e event arrives.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA capture event is rejected — with a warning, keeping the rest of the stream — when it carries something \u003ccode\u003eingest\u003c/code\u003e would refuse, so a trace can always be restored from its own export: a \u003ccode\u003etrace_id\u003c/code\u003e that is not an identifier (empty, or carrying control characters), a step with no name, non-string tags, a decision \u003ccode\u003econfidence\u003c/code\u003e outside 0–1, and decision \u003ccode\u003eoptions\u003c/code\u003e that are not \u003ccode\u003e{option, …}\u003c/code\u003e objects. Usage and timing fields that are not non-negative finite numbers are dropped the same way.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# Pipe a JSONL event stream into the recorder\nmy-agent --emit-events | agent-replay record --tags production\n\n# Keep the trace open (don't finalize as timeout) when the stream ends\nmy-agent --emit-events | agent-replay record --leave-open\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Pipe a JSONL event stream into the recorder\u003c/span\u003e\nmy-agent --emit-events \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e|\u003c/span\u003e agent-replay record --tags production\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Keep the trace open (don't finalize as timeout) when the stream ends\u003c/span\u003e\nmy-agent --emit-events \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e|\u003c/span\u003e agent-replay record --leave-open\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003erecord\u003c/code\u003e also speaks the major CLIs' own non-interactive streams directly, so you can pipe them in without instrumentation:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"codex exec --json \u0026quot;fix the failing tests\u0026quot;      | agent-replay record --format codex-exec\ngemini -p \u0026quot;summarize\u0026quot; --output-format stream-json | agent-replay record --format gemini-stream\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003ecodex \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eexec\u003c/span\u003e --json \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003efix the failing tests\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e      \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e|\u003c/span\u003e agent-replay record --format codex-exec\ngemini -p \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003esummarize\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e --output-format stream-json \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e|\u003c/span\u003e agent-replay record --format gemini-stream\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor the native protocol, each event is one JSON object on its own line carrying \u003ccode\u003ev: 1\u003c/code\u003e, a \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e, and (except \u003ccode\u003etrace_start\u003c/code\u003e) the \u003ccode\u003etrace_id\u003c/code\u003e the producer generated:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eEvent\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003ePurpose\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrace_start\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eOpen a trace (\u003ccode\u003eagent_name\u003c/code\u003e required; optional \u003ccode\u003etrace_id\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003esession_id\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003einput\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etags\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estep_start\u003c/code\u003e / \u003ccode\u003estep_end\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eOpen a step, then close it with output/error/timing/tokens\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estep\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA complete step in one event (may include a \u003ccode\u003edecision\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003esnapshot\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edecision\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAttach a decision record to a step (any step type)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esnapshot\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eFreeze context/environment/tool state at a step\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etrace_end\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eFinalize the trace (\u003ccode\u003estatus\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eoutput\u003c/code\u003e, token/cost totals)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAn unknown event \u003cem\u003etype\u003c/em\u003e is skipped with a warning; an unknown \u003cem\u003efield\u003c/em\u003e is ignored silently, so a newer producer's extra keys cost nothing and neither case is ever a crash. A usage or timing field that is not a non-negative finite number (\u003ccode\u003etokens_used\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eduration_ms\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etotal_tokens\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etotal_duration_ms\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etotal_cost_usd\u003c/code\u003e) is dropped with a warning and the rest of the event is kept, since \u003ccode\u003eingest\u003c/code\u003e rejects such a value and the trace would otherwise be unrestorable from its own export. A trace left open when the stream ends is finalized as \u003ccode\u003etimeout\u003c/code\u003e unless \u003ccode\u003e--leave-open\u003c/code\u003e — including one this stream resumed by id, so a trace can't dangle silently. The single exception is the trace a \u003cem\u003elive\u003c/em\u003e enclosing \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay run\u003c/code\u003e handed down (via \u003ccode\u003eAGENT_REPLAY_TRACE_ID\u003c/code\u003e): that one belongs to the wrapper, which finalizes it from the child's exit.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eOpenTelemetry ingest\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-opentelemetry-ingest\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: OpenTelemetry ingest\" href=\"#opentelemetry-ingest\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMany agent stacks already emit OpenTelemetry with the GenAI semantic conventions (\u003ccode\u003egen_ai.*\u003c/code\u003e) — Gemini CLI, Claude Code, OpenHands, Goose, AutoGen, and most Python frameworks via OpenInference/OpenLLMetry. Run a local OTLP receiver and point them at it, no per-framework adapter needed:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"agent-replay otel serve --port 4318\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eagent-replay otel serve --port 4318\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt accepts \u003ccode\u003ePOST /v1/traces\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ePOST /v1/logs\u003c/code\u003e, each in both OTLP/JSON and OTLP/protobuf, with gzip. Spans map onto the trace model: \u003ccode\u003einvoke_agent\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003einvoke_workflow\u003c/code\u003e roots become traces (\u003ccode\u003egen_ai.agent.name\u003c/code\u003e → agent, \u003ccode\u003egen_ai.conversation.id\u003c/code\u003e → session), \u003ccode\u003eexecute_tool\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003etool_call\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003echat\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003egenerate_content\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003etext_completion\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003ellm_call\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eembeddings\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eretrieval\u003c/code\u003e → \u003ccode\u003eretrieval\u003c/code\u003e, span parentage → step hierarchy, and \u003ccode\u003egen_ai.usage.*\u003c/code\u003e → token totals. Deprecated attribute forms (\u003ccode\u003egen_ai.system\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eprompt_tokens\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ecompletion_tokens\u003c/code\u003e) are normalized. The two other common dialects are read for content as well as classification: OpenInference (\u003ccode\u003eopeninference.span.kind\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003einput.value\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eoutput.value\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ellm.prompts\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ellm.completions\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ellm.provider\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ellm.model_name\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ellm.token_count.*\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etool.name\u003c/code\u003e) and OpenLLMetry (\u003ccode\u003etraceloop.span.kind\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etraceloop.entity.input\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003eoutput\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etraceloop.entity.name\u003c/code\u003e), so a LangChain or LlamaIndex app records prompts and responses, not just span shapes. Spans without an agent root are grouped into a synthetic trace per OTel trace ID. Spans (and log events) of one trace that arrive across several export batches — the usual case, as a \u003ccode\u003eBatchSpanProcessor\u003c/code\u003e flushes finished child spans before the root ends — are assembled into a single trace by OTel trace ID (log events by session ID), and the rootless synthetic trace is upgraded in place once the root batch arrives; each batch is still stored on arrival, so the trace stays queryable mid-session. Steps of an assembled trace are numbered by span start time rather than arrival order, so a parent span that flushes after its children still comes before them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA batch an exporter \u003cstrong\u003eredelivers\u003c/strong\u003e (a lost \u003ccode\u003e200\u003c/code\u003e, a client timeout after the write, an exporter retry) is recognized on the span path and not stored twice: spans already on the trace are dropped by span id, and the batch's tokens and cost are recomputed from the spans it actually contributes — including a mixed batch that redelivers the token-carrying span alongside a new one, so a retry cannot inflate the totals. The \u003cstrong\u003elog\u003c/strong\u003e path has no equivalent identity — a log record carries no span id — so redelivered log batches can still duplicate; prefer at-most-once delivery there, or use the span endpoint.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLog events from the two CLIs that emit richer signal as logs are mapped too: Gemini CLI (\u003ccode\u003egemini_cli.user_prompt\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egemini_cli.tool_call\u003c/code\u003e — including its \u003ccode\u003edecision\u003c/code\u003e as a decision record attributed to user or policy, \u003ccode\u003egemini_cli.api_response\u003c/code\u003e tokens) and Claude Code (\u003ccode\u003eclaude_code.*\u003c/code\u003e), correlated by \u003ccode\u003esession.id\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePoint an exporter at it over HTTP/JSON. Most emitters default to gRPC on port 4317, so switch them to HTTP:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGemini CLI\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003etelemetry: { enabled: true, target: \"local\", otlpEndpoint: \"http://localhost:4318\", otlpProtocol: \"http\" }\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClaude Code\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003eCLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318\u003c/code\u003e (opt into content with \u003ccode\u003eOTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGoose / OpenHands\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003eOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBoth CLIs redact prompt/response content unless you opt in on their side (Gemini \u003ccode\u003etelemetry.logPrompts\u003c/code\u003e, Claude Code \u003ccode\u003eOTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1\u003c/code\u003e); \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay\u003c/code\u003e records whatever they send.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eGenAI, OpenInference, and OpenLLMetry span dialects are all recognized, including their prompt/response content. Both \u003ccode\u003e/v1/traces\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e/v1/logs\u003c/code\u003e accept OTLP/JSON and OTLP/protobuf, so an exporter left on its default protobuf protocol works without reconfiguring it to JSON.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eHook capture\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-hook-capture\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Hook capture\" href=\"#hook-capture\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eagent-replay hook\u003c/code\u003e plugs into the stdin-JSON hook convention shared by Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI. It's stateless — each invocation correlates to a trace by the payload's \u003ccode\u003esession_id\u003c/code\u003e — and auto-detects the dialect, so no flag is needed. Capture is side-effect-only: it always exits 0 and writes nothing to stdout (in these harnesses exit 2 blocks the agent and stdout is read as a hook decision), so it can never interfere with a run. Add \u003ccode\u003e--no-input\u003c/code\u003e to drop prompt text and tool inputs on shared machines.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClaude Code\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e~/.claude/settings.json\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"{\n  \u0026quot;hooks\u0026quot;: {\n    \u0026quot;UserPromptSubmit\u0026quot;: [{ \u0026quot;hooks\u0026quot;: [{ \u0026quot;type\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;command\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;command\u0026quot;: \u0026quot;agent-replay hook\u0026quot; }] }],\n    \u0026quot;PreToolUse\u0026quot;:  [{ \u0026quot;hooks\u0026quot;: [{ history that already exists on disk, \u003ccode\u003eimport\u003c/code\u003e converts a Claude Code transcript or a Codex CLI rollout into a trace. It's best-effort: unrecognized records are skipped and counted (both vendor formats are internal and version-unstable), and the source format/version is stamped in the trace metadata.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"agent-replay import ~/.claude/projects/my-project/\u0026lt;session-uuid\u0026gt;.jsonl --format claude-transcript\nagent-replay import ~/.codex/sessions/2026/07/02/rollout-abc.jsonl      --format codex-rollout\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eagent-replay import \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e~\u003c/span\u003e/.claude/projects/my-project/\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003esession-uuid\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e.jsonl --format claude-transcript\nagent-replay import \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e~\u003c/span\u003e/.codex/sessions/2026/07/02/rollout-abc.jsonl      --format codex-rollout\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor Claude Code, \u003ccode\u003etool_use\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003etool_result\u003c/code\u003e blocks become paired \u003ccode\u003etool_call\u003c/code\u003e steps (a result flagged \u003ccode\u003eis_error\u003c/code\u003e records its message on the step's error field, so a failed tool call stays distinguishable from a successful one), \u003ccode\u003ethinking\u003c/code\u003e blocks become \u003ccode\u003ethought\u003c/code\u003e steps, and \u003ccode\u003eusage\u003c/code\u003e counts aggregate into token totals — including the two cache fields, which is where most of a real session's consumption lives. For Codex, \u003ccode\u003esession_meta\u003c/code\u003e supplies identity and git metadata, both tool families (\u003ccode\u003efunction_call\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003efunction_call_output\u003c/code\u003e and the freeform \u003ccode\u003ecustom_tool_call\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003ecustom_tool_call_output\u003c/code\u003e, each paired by \u003ccode\u003ecall_id\u003c/code\u003e) become \u003ccode\u003etool_call\u003c/code\u003e steps with a non-zero exit code or an explicit failure recorded on the step's error field, \u003ccode\u003ereasoning\u003c/code\u003e becomes \u003ccode\u003ethought\u003c/code\u003e steps, and \u003ccode\u003etoken_count\u003c/code\u003e supplies the session token total.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA session's user turns are all kept: one becomes the trace input, later ones go to \u003ccode\u003emetadata.follow_up_prompts\u003c/code\u003e, and any harness preamble ahead of the prompt goes to \u003ccode\u003emetadata.preamble_prompts\u003c/code\u003e. Real transcripts usually open with an envelope (a slash-command block, injected instructions, an environment or plugin preamble, a system reminder), so the prompt is the first turn that isn't one — detected by shape, since a person's question essentially never opens with \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/code\u003e. An envelope prompt is still used if that is all the session has.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eImporting the same session twice does \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e create a second trace:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"agent-replay import \u0026lt;same-file\u0026gt;              # \u0026quot;Session already imported as trc_… — nothing changed.\u0026quot;\nagent-replay import \u0026lt;same-file\u0026gt; --replace    # re-import it (use this when the transcript has grown)\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eagent-replay import \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003esame-file\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e              \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e \"Session already imported as trc_… — nothing changed.\"\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay import \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003esame-file\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e --replace    \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e re-import it (use this when the transcript has grown)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTranscripts are read a line at a time rather than loaded whole, so peak memory tracks the trace being built rather than the file: a 52 MB session imports in ~270 MB instead of ~440 MB, and a session larger than ~512 MB imports at all (it previously failed with \"Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters\" and no partial import — a 647 MB transcript now imports its 672,000 steps).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSessions are identified by session id, source format \u003cstrong\u003eand\u003c/strong\u003e source filename — a Claude Code subagent sidecar (\u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;session\u0026gt;/subagents/agent-*.jsonl\u003c/code\u003e) carries the same session id as its parent transcript, so the file has to be part of the identity. A file that carries no session id is imported each time it is named, and a trace imported before this identity existed is never replaced.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eEnforcement (block dangerous tool calls live)\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-enforcement-block-dangerous-tool-calls-live\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Enforcement (block dangerous tool calls live)\" href=\"#enforcement-block-dangerous-tool-calls-live\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAdd \u003ccode\u003e--enforce\u003c/code\u003e to the hook to evaluate each proposed tool call against your \u003ca href=\"#guardrails\"\u003eguardrail policies\u003c/a\u003e before it runs, and block denied calls in the harness's own dialect. Register it with the event name — \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay hook PreToolUse --enforce\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003eBeforeTool\u003c/code\u003e for Gemini CLI) — so that if stdin arrives empty or unreadable, the command still knows a tool call was being gated and blocks rather than allowing an unchecked call. It also needs to find your store: the path resolves from the hook process's working directory, so pass \u003ccode\u003e--dir\u003c/code\u003e unless that is the project root.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAn enforcing gate that cannot fire fails closed rather than passing everything — in \u003ccode\u003ehook --enforce\u003c/code\u003e and in \u003ccode\u003eguard check\u003c/code\u003e alike. Enforcing against a store that does not exist blocks with the reason, and so does enforcing against a store with \u003cstrong\u003eno enabled policies\u003c/strong\u003e — otherwise a capture hook running from the wrong directory creates an empty store, and every tool call after it is allowed silently while the setup still looks correct. If you want \u003ccode\u003e--enforce\u003c/code\u003e registered before you have written any policies, pass \u003ccode\u003e--allow-empty\u003c/code\u003e to say so.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eClaude Code / Codex CLI\u003c/strong\u003e: emits \u003ccode\u003e{\"hookSpecificOutput\": {\"permissionDecision\": \"deny\" | \"ask\", ...}}\u003c/code\u003e — \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e policies block, \u003ccode\u003erequire_review\u003c/code\u003e policies defer to the harness's own approval prompt (\u003ccode\u003e\"ask\"\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGemini CLI\u003c/strong\u003e: emits \u003ccode\u003e{\"decision\": \"deny\", \"reason\": ...}\u003c/code\u003e (its hooks are allow/deny only, so \u003ccode\u003erequire_review\u003c/code\u003e denies with a \"review required\" reason).\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCrush / others without structured output\u003c/strong\u003e: exits 2 with the reason on stderr. The dialect is detected from the payload, and nothing in a payload identifies a harness that doesn't read hook stdout — so declare it with \u003ccode\u003e--dialect other\u003c/code\u003e (also \u003ccode\u003eclaude-code\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egemini\u003c/code\u003e to pin detection), and denied calls are answered by exit code alone.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ewarn\u003c/code\u003e policies never block — they surface a message and allow the call. Every enforcement decision that matches a policy is recorded as a \u003ccode\u003eguard_check\u003c/code\u003e step in the session's trace, linked to the attempted \u003ccode\u003etool_call\u003c/code\u003e, so blocked attempts show up in \u003ca href=\"#inspect\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eshow\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"#explain-decisions\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ewhy\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou can also evaluate a single step out of band:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"echo '{\u0026quot;step_type\u0026quot;:\u0026quot;tool_call\u0026quot;,\u0026quot;name\u0026quot;:\u0026quot;delete_user\u0026quot;}' | agent-replay guard check   # exit 2 if denied\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eecho\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e{\"step_type\":\"tool_call\",\"name\":\"delete_user\"}\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e'\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e|\u003c/span\u003e agent-replay guard check   \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e exit 2 if denied\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIt prints a machine-readable verdict on stdout — \u003ccode\u003e{\"action\", \"policy\", \"reason\"}\u003c/code\u003e\n— with the human-readable line on stderr, so it scripts cleanly:\n\u003ccode\u003e{\"action\":\"deny\",\"policy\":\"no-deletes\",\"reason\":\"...\"}\u003c/code\u003e on a block,\n\u003ccode\u003e{\"action\":\"allow\",\"policy\":null,\"reason\":null}\u003c/code\u003e otherwise. Standalone,\n\u003ccode\u003erequire_review\u003c/code\u003e prompts when a TTY is present and otherwise fails closed,\nreporting \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e with a \"review required (no TTY — failed closed)\" reason.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGuardrail, not a boundary.\u003c/strong\u003e Hook-level enforcement is a guardrail, not a complete security boundary — the harness vendors say so themselves (a determined agent can often reach equivalent effects through another tool path). For hard isolation, use OS-level sandboxing: Claude Code's sandbox, Codex \u003ccode\u003esandbox_mode\u003c/code\u003e, or Gemini CLI's sandbox.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eBrowse\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-browse\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Browse\" href=\"#browse\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# List the most recent traces (25 at a time by default; the header\n# reports the full count, and --limit raises the page size)\nagent-replay list\n\n# Filter by status, agent, tag, or time\nagent-replay list --status failed\nagent-replay list --agent travel-bot --since 7d\nagent-replay list --tag production --sort -tokens --limit 10\n\n# JSON output for piping\nagent-replay list --json\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e List the most recent traces (25 at a time by default; the header\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e reports the full count, and --limit raises the page size)\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay list\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Filter by status, agent, tag, or time\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay list --status failed\nagent-replay list --agent travel-bot --since 7d\nagent-replay list --tag production --sort -tokens --limit 10\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e JSON output for piping\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay list --json\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAn \u003cstrong\u003eempty\u003c/strong\u003e value for \u003ccode\u003e--status\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e--agent\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e--tag\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e--session\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e--since\u003c/code\u003e is\na usage error (exit \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e), not an unfiltered listing — so a filter built from an\nunset shell variable (\u003ccode\u003elist --agent \"$AGENT\"\u003c/code\u003e) fails loudly instead of quietly\nreturning every trace at exit \u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e, which reads exactly like a correct narrow\nresult.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--agent\u003c/code\u003e matches by \u003cstrong\u003esubstring\u003c/strong\u003e, so \u003ccode\u003e--agent travel\u003c/code\u003e finds \u003ccode\u003etravel-bot\u003c/code\u003e and\n\u003ccode\u003etravel-assistant\u003c/code\u003e alike; \u003ccode\u003e--session\u003c/code\u003e matches by \u003cstrong\u003eprefix\u003c/strong\u003e, like a trace id.\nConvenient for browsing, but worth knowing wherever the selection decides a\nverdict: \u003ccode\u003echeck --golden --agent travel-bot\u003c/code\u003e in a store that also holds\n\u003ccode\u003etravel-bot-v2\u003c/code\u003e traces checks both. For a CI gate, prefer \u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003echeck --agent-exact \u0026lt;name\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e, which selects only that agent — a substring is right for browsing and wrong for a gate, because under \u003ccode\u003e--strict\u003c/code\u003e an unrelated agent that happens to contain the term decides the verdict. Pair it with a baseline exported for the same agent, or the other baselines count as unexercised. The two flags are mutually exclusive.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWith no \u003ccode\u003e--sort\u003c/code\u003e at all, traces are listed newest first. Passing \u003ccode\u003e--sort\u003c/code\u003e orders\nascending; prefix the field with \u003ccode\u003e-\u003c/code\u003e for descending. So \"my ten most expensive\nruns\" is \u003ccode\u003e--sort -tokens --limit 10\u003c/code\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e--sort tokens\u003c/code\u003e returns the cheapest ten,\nand \u003ccode\u003e--sort started_at\u003c/code\u003e returns the \u003cem\u003eoldest\u003c/em\u003e first, reversing the default view.\nSortable fields: \u003ccode\u003estarted_at\u003c/code\u003e (the default field), \u003ccode\u003eduration\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etokens\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecost\u003c/code\u003e,\n\u003ccode\u003eagent_name\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003eA windowed \u003ccode\u003eshow --json\u003c/code\u003e carries a \u003ccode\u003estep_window\u003c/code\u003e object (\u003ccode\u003efrom\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eto\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eshown\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eomitted\u003c/code\u003e) so a consumer can tell a subset from a whole trace; an unwindowed one has no such field.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTrace IDs support prefix matching — just type the first few characters. A prefix that matches more than one trace is an error naming the candidates, not a silent pick, so a command never answers about (or, in \u003ccode\u003efork\u003c/code\u003e's case, writes from) a trace you did not name.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWatch a live run\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-watch-a-live-run\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Watch a live run\" href=\"#watch-a-live-run\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhile a trace is still being captured — by \u003ccode\u003ehook\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erecord\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erun\u003c/code\u003e, or the OTel receiver — \u003ccode\u003ewatch\u003c/code\u003e live-tails it, printing each new step as it lands:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# Follow the most recent still-running trace\nagent-replay watch\n\n# Follow a specific trace, polling faster\nagent-replay watch \u0026lt;trace-id\u0026gt; --interval 200\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Follow the most recent still-running trace\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay watch\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Follow a specific trace, polling faster\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay watch \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003etrace-id\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e --interval 200\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWith no id it picks the most recent \u003ccode\u003erunning\u003c/code\u003e trace — by start \u003cem\u003einstant\u003c/em\u003e, not by the spelling of the timestamp — so it's the natural companion to a hook-instrumented session in another terminal. It exits when the trace is finalized.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--interval\u003c/code\u003e is in milliseconds and is capped at \u003ccode\u003e2147483647\u003c/code\u003e ms — above that\nNode's timer overflows and clamps to 1 ms, polling the database about a\nthousand times a second rather than almost never, so it is a usage error (exit\n\u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e) instead.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA producer that opens a step and closes it later (the two-phase \u003ccode\u003estep_start\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003estep_end\u003c/code\u003e protocol) gets two lines per step: the announcement when the step starts, and a closing line carrying what only the end knows — duration, tokens, and any error. A producer that writes a complete step in one event gets a single line. Text that came from the agent (step names, errors, models, decision rationales) is escaped before it reaches your terminal, so a control sequence in a tool's stderr cannot retarget the terminal you are watching from.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eExplain decisions\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-explain-decisions\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Explain decisions\" href=\"#explain-decisions\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen a trace records \u003cem\u003ewhy\u003c/em\u003e it acted — decision alternatives, causal links between steps, and step hierarchy — you can inspect that structure directly.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# Walk the causal chain backward from a step to the decision that triggered it\nagent-replay why \u0026lt;trace-id\u0026gt; on \u003ccode\u003estep_type\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ename\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003einput\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eoutput\u003c/code\u003e, with \u003ccode\u003e--modify-input\u003c/code\u003e shows the input you\nchanged. Trace-level differences report a step of \u003ccode\u003etrace\u003c/code\u003e (\u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e in \u003ccode\u003e--json\u003c/code\u003e)\nand never set \u003ccode\u003edivergence_step\u003c/code\u003e, which means \"the first step that went\ndifferent\". Steps are paired by \u003ccode\u003estep_number\u003c/code\u003e, so gaps don't misalign the\ncomparison. Narrow the comparison with \u003ccode\u003e--fields\u003c/code\u003e; when a filter leaves nothing,\nthe verdict says so rather than claiming the traces are identical, and a filter\nnaming no field at all is a usage error.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003edecision\u003c/code\u003e compares the chosen option, its rationale, and who decided — so two\nruns that took opposite actions at the same step are reported as different even\nwhen every other field matches. Confidence and the option list are deliberately\nexcluded: they are the model's self-report and vary run to run without the agent\nhaving acted differently.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv agent.js\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe wrapper pre-creates a trace and hands the child a recording channel via environment variables (\u003ccode\u003eAGENT_REPLAY_DIR\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eAGENT_REPLAY_TRACE_ID\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eAGENT_REPLAY_EVENTS\u003c/code\u003e). Every \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay\u003c/code\u003e command honors \u003ccode\u003eAGENT_REPLAY_DIR\u003c/code\u003e as its data directory when \u003ccode\u003e--dir\u003c/code\u003e isn't given, so a nested invocation (\u003ccode\u003erun -- sh -c '... | agent-replay record'\u003c/code\u003e) writes to the wrapper's store rather than a fresh one in the working directory. An instrumented child (using the \u003ca href=\"#programmatic-api\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eTraceRecorder\u003c/code\u003e SDK\u003c/a\u003e or writing JSONL events to \u003ccode\u003e$AGENT_REPLAY_EVENTS\u003c/code\u003e) records a full step-by-step trace; an uninstrumented child still gets a trace with timing and exit metadata. The child's stdio passes through untouched, and the trace is finalized from its exit — \u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e → completed, non-zero → failed with the code recorded. A child that sends its own \u003ccode\u003etrace_end\u003c/code\u003e owns the status: that declaration is kept even when it disagrees with the exit code, and the summary names both (\u003ccode\u003ecompleted (child exited 7)\u003c/code\u003e). \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay run\u003c/code\u003e exits with the child's own status either way, so it drops cleanly into scripts and CI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe events channel is \u003cstrong\u003eappend-only\u003c/strong\u003e: open it with \u003ccode\u003ea\u003c/code\u003e, never \u003ccode\u003ew\u003c/code\u003e. A producer that rewrites it is detected and warned about, but events written before the rewrite are gone. If the store refuses an event (a child recording several sub-traces collides on per-trace step numbering), the run summary says how many could not be stored.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eRegression check (CI)\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-regression-check-ci\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Regression check (CI)\" href=\"#regression-check-ci\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTurn known-good runs into a regression gate. Export a golden dataset once, then \u003ccode\u003echeck\u003c/code\u003e new runs against it — the comparison is structural (step count, step types and names, tool-call inputs, final status) rather than raw output text, so non-deterministic wording never causes false failures. It exits non-zero on any regression, ready for CI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" golden.json --fields step_types,decisions\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eComparable fields: \u003ccode\u003estep_count\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estep_types\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estep_names\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003etool_inputs\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estep_errors\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estatus\u003c/code\u003e (the default set), plus opt-in \u003ccode\u003emodel\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003edecisions\u003c/code\u003e. \u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003edecisions\u003c/code\u003e compares the option each step CHOSE\u003c/strong\u003e — the divergence a structural gate is otherwise blind to: rename nothing, change no tool, and swap \u003ccode\u003eescalate_to_human\u003c/code\u003e for \u003ccode\u003edelete_records\u003c/code\u003e, and every default field still matches. It is opt-in because no baseline exported before it carries the data, so making it a default would turn a working gate into the \"nothing to compare\" refusal on upgrade; re-export the baseline and pass \u003ccode\u003e--fields ...,decisions\u003c/code\u003e. Only a step the baseline recorded a decision for is compared. \u003ccode\u003estep_errors\u003c/code\u003e compares whether each step FAILED — a step that starts erroring is a regression the other fields cannot see, since a hook-captured session finalizes \u003ccode\u003ecompleted\u003c/code\u003e from its Stop event however many tool calls failed inside it. It is one-directional: a step that \u003cem\u003estops\u003c/em\u003e failing is a fix, not a regression. Only the flag is compared, never the message, and a baseline exported before this field is skipped step by step. An unrecognized \u003ccode\u003e--fields\u003c/code\u003e value is rejected rather than silently comparing nothing — as a usage error (exit \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e) named for the bad field, checked before the store is opened, so a typo can't surface as \"no traces matched\" instead. A \u003cem\u003evalid\u003c/em\u003e field that no baseline entry can exercise (\u003ccode\u003e--fields model\u003c/code\u003e against a baseline captured without per-step models) is refused the same way, for the same reason: it would otherwise compare nothing and report a pass. This is judged per candidate, so a mixed run in which one agent has no tool calls refuses \u003ccode\u003e--fields tool_inputs\u003c/code\u003e for the whole run rather than passing on another agent's behalf — narrow the run with \u003ccode\u003e--agent\u003c/code\u003e if that is not what you want.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA golden entry also carries \u003ccode\u003eexpected_output\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eeval_criteria\u003c/code\u003e. These are recorded for downstream consumers and human review — \u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003echeck\u003c/code\u003e does not compare them\u003c/strong\u003e; the gate is structural, over the fields listed above. \u003ccode\u003emetadata\u003c/code\u003e is required, though: an entry without \u003ccode\u003emetadata.status\u003c/code\u003e is refused, because the \u003ccode\u003estatus\u003c/code\u003e comparison would otherwise be silently skipped.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCandidates gathered in bulk are the runs that could actually regress: \u003cstrong\u003eforks and still-\u003ccode\u003erunning\u003c/code\u003e traces are excluded\u003c/strong\u003e. A fork is a never-executed copy of a step prefix, so it matches its own baseline and then \"diverges\" on step count and status — one \u003ccode\u003efork\u003c/code\u003e would otherwise turn the gate permanently red on a shared store. A running trace is mid-flight, so its partial shape is not a regression either. A trace named explicitly with \u003ccode\u003e--trace\u003c/code\u003e is always compared, whatever its lineage or status. For the same reason, \u003ccode\u003eexport --format golden\u003c/code\u003e leaves forks out of a baseline, while \u003ccode\u003ejson\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ejsonl\u003c/code\u003e exports are backups and keep them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMatches are made by agent name and a hash of the input, so each run is compared to its own golden counterpart. A divergence report names the trace, the step, and the differing field. The summary also reports baseline entries \u003cstrong\u003eno candidate exercised\u003c/strong\u003e — a scenario whose run crashed or never happened at all, which otherwise leaves a gate green with nothing to say about it. Those count as failures under \u003ccode\u003e--strict\u003c/code\u003e, alongside unmatched runs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBuild the baseline from runs that finished cleanly: \u003ccode\u003eexport --format golden\u003c/code\u003e warns when entries did not come from a completed run — a \u003ccode\u003erunning\u003c/code\u003e trace bakes in a partial shape the next correct run \"regresses\" against, and a \u003ccode\u003efailed\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003etimeout\u003c/code\u003e one makes reproducing the failure pass green. The warning reports how many of the entries that covers, not which condition each hit; filter with \u003ccode\u003e--tag known-good\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e--status completed\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA gate that cannot do its job fails loudly (exit \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e) instead of passing green. That covers a golden file with no entries — an empty baseline can never detect a regression, and the usual cause is an export filter that matched nothing, which the export warns about too — a file that isn't a golden dataset at all (\u003ccode\u003e--format json\u003c/code\u003e output is a common mix-up), and a run where no trace matched the filters, whether from a mistyped \u003ccode\u003e--agent\u003c/code\u003e, a \u003ccode\u003e--since\u003c/code\u003e window that outran the recording, or a \u003ccode\u003e--dir\u003c/code\u003e pointing somewhere the runs were never recorded. The same is true when candidates exist but NONE of them matched a baseline: nothing was compared, so nothing could regress. That usually means the agent was renamed, the input template changed, or capture stopped recording the input (\u003ccode\u003ehook --no-input\u003c/code\u003e) — all of which change the match key. \u003ccode\u003e--strict\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e--trace\u003c/code\u003e keep their own verdicts (a regression, and a plain unmatched report). If either empty case is expected — a quiet nightly window, a matrix job where this agent didn't run — pass \u003ccode\u003e--allow-empty\u003c/code\u003e, which opts out of both refusals. With \u003ccode\u003e--json\u003c/code\u003e, a refusal is reported as \u003ccode\u003e{\"ok\": false, \"error\": ...}\u003c/code\u003e rather than bare stderr, so a \u003ccode\u003echeck --json | jq -r .ok\u003c/code\u003e pipeline still reads a verdict.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" an unusable pattern (an invalid or unsafe\n\u003ccode\u003ename_regex\u003c/code\u003e, a non-string match value, a \u003ccode\u003estep_type\u003c/code\u003e that isn't a real step type\n— e.g. in a form that\nsilently fails to match. If a malformed policy is somehow\npresent anyway, a \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e/\u003ccode\u003erequire_review\u003c/code\u003e policy fails \u003cem\u003eclosed\u003c/em\u003e (treats the step\nas a match) rather than letting it through. The one exception is a completely\nempty pattern, which stays inert even for a \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e: it expresses no intent to\nfilter, and blocking every step would be worse than the misconfiguration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eoutput_contains\u003c/code\u003e cannot block live.\u003c/strong\u003e Enforcement evaluates a \u003cem\u003eproposed\u003c/em\u003e tool\ncall — before it runs, so it has no output yet — and every match key in a pattern\nmust match. A \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003erequire_review\u003c/code\u003e keyed on \u003ccode\u003eoutput_contains\u003c/code\u003e therefore\nnever fires under \u003ccode\u003ehook --enforce\u003c/code\u003e, no matter how it looks in \u003ccode\u003eguard list\u003c/code\u003e. It\nstill matches in post-hoc evaluation (\u003ccode\u003eguard test\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eguard check\u003c/code\u003e on a\nrecorded step), so it is a useful auditing pattern, not a blocking one; \u003ccode\u003eguard add\u003c/code\u003e warns when you write one as a blocking policy.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe most restrictive match wins.\u003c/strong\u003e When several policies match one step, the\nverdict is the strictest of them — \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e over \u003ccode\u003erequire_review\u003c/code\u003e over \u003ccode\u003ewarn\u003c/code\u003e over\n\u003ccode\u003eallow\u003c/code\u003e — and \u003ccode\u003e--priority\u003c/code\u003e only breaks ties \u003cem\u003eamong equally restrictive\u003c/em\u003e matches,\ndeciding which policy is cited. So a broad \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e plus a narrow, higher-priority\n\u003ccode\u003eallow\u003c/code\u003e does \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e carve out an exception: the call is still denied. Express an\nexception by narrowing the \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e pattern itself.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003einput_contains\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eoutput_contains\u003c/code\u003e match against both the raw text and the\nJSON form of the step's input/output, so a pattern containing quotes,\nbackslashes, newlines, or tabs matches as written — \u003ccode\u003erm -rf \"/etc\"\u003c/code\u003e and\n\u003ccode\u003eC:\\Windows\\System32\u003c/code\u003e both work, as do patterns aimed at the JSON itself like\n\u003ccode\u003e\"cmd\"\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003eGOOGLE_API_KEY\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eOPENAI_API_KEY\u003c/code\u003e. Environment variables take priority over config file values.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eai.max_tokens\u003c/code\u003e caps the judge's reply (default 1024) and is what the \u003ccode\u003e--max-cost\u003c/code\u003e estimate prices, so raising it raises both the ceiling and the quoted cost. \u003ccode\u003eai.model\u003c/code\u003e is only applied to a provider it belongs to — a \u003ccode\u003eclaude-*\u003c/code\u003e model is never sent to OpenAI.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003econfig set\u003c/code\u003e refuses an \u003cstrong\u003eempty\u003c/strong\u003e value (exit \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e): a blank key was stored, then\ndisplayed as \u003ccode\u003e***\u003c/code\u003e by \u003ccode\u003econfig get\u003c/code\u003e — looking set — while every check downstream\ntreated it as unset, so \u003ccode\u003etest-ai\u003c/code\u003e told you to set the key you had just set. To\nclear a value, re-run \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay init --force\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA config file that exists but \u003cstrong\u003ecannot be parsed\u003c/strong\u003e is reported as its own error,\nnaming the file and the parse position, rather than as \"no configuration found\"\n— which used to send you to \u003ccode\u003einit\u003c/code\u003e, which then said the store was already\ninitialized. \u003ccode\u003econfig set\u003c/code\u003e also writes back only the key you named: a value it\nhad to ignore (say a \u003ccode\u003eai.max_tokens\u003c/code\u003e typed as a string) stays on disk, so it is\nstill reported and still fixable.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003etraces.db\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003econfig.json\u003c/code\u003e are created owner-only (\u003ccode\u003e0600\u003c/code\u003e) — a trace holds\nprompts, tool inputs and tool outputs, and the config holds API keys in\nplaintext. A directory \u003ccode\u003eagent-replay\u003c/code\u003e creates for itself is \u003ccode\u003e0700\u003c/code\u003e as well; a\ndirectory that already exists is left exactly as you set it, since the mode of a\ndirectory you made is your decision. The file modes are set at creation only, so\nif you deliberately open a store up it stays open.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" CI:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eCode\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eMeaning\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSuccess — including \"no matches\" for queries like \u003ccode\u003elist\u003c/code\u003e and empty exports.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eRuntime failure — trace not found, a malformed ingest, a \u003ccode\u003erecord\u003c/code\u003e stream whose every event was rejected, an \u003ccode\u003eimport\u003c/code\u003e that found nothing to import (no steps and no prompt), a \u003ccode\u003echeck --golden\u003c/code\u003e regression, or an \u003ccode\u003eeval\u003c/code\u003e that fails (a rubric below its threshold or a built-in preset that fails).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eUsage error, or a command refusing an environment it cannot run in (\u003ccode\u003edashboard\u003c/code\u003e without an interactive terminal) — an unknown flag, an unknown command, a missing, empty or bad argument value, or an unexpected extra argument (a typo'd second id or a bare word meant to be a flag is rejected, not silently ignored). Also the \u003cstrong\u003eguard block\u003c/strong\u003e signal: \u003ccode\u003eguard check\u003c/code\u003e exits \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e when a policy denies a step (the harness \"block\" convention), as does \u003ccode\u003ehook --enforce --dialect other\u003c/code\u003e. \u003ccode\u003eguard check\u003c/code\u003e fails closed, so it also answers \u003ccode\u003e2\u003c/code\u003e — with a \u003ccode\u003edeny\u003c/code\u003e verdict on stdout — for a step it cannot evaluate at all: unreadable or malformed stdin, a payload that isn't a step object, a missing \u003ccode\u003estep_type\u003c/code\u003e, a store it cannot open, or a store holding no enabled policies (a gate that can never fire; pass \u003ccode\u003e--allow-empty\u003c/code\u003e if that is deliberate). For a detected harness dialect, \u003ccode\u003ehook --enforce\u003c/code\u003e answers with that harness's own JSON on stdout and exits \u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e — the block is the JSON, not the code — so don't gate a script on \u003ccode\u003e$?\u003c/code\u003e there.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTwo commands instead propagate a child's own status: \u003ccode\u003erun\u003c/code\u003e exits with the wrapped command's exit code, and \u003ccode\u003ehook\u003c/code\u003e (capture mode) always exits \u003ccode\u003e0\u003c/code\u003e so it can never interfere with the host agent.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUnder \u003ccode\u003e--json\u003c/code\u003e, a failure is still answered \u003cstrong\u003eas JSON on stdout\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003e{\"ok\": false, \"error\": \"...\", \"hints\": [...]}\u003c/code\u003e — so a \u003ccode\u003e| jq\u003c/code\u003e pipeline gets a document it can read on every outcome rather than a parse error. The exit code is unchanged by the output shape.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvaluation dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ehallucination-check\u003c/strong\u003e — Detects hallucination indicators:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eFlags excessive hedging language (30%)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eChecks if output is grounded in retrieval content (40%)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eVerifies no failed steps and no trace-level error (30%, \u003cstrong\u003ecritical\u003c/strong\u003e only when the run itself ended badly — see below)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThreshold: 0.7\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003esafety-check\u003c/strong\u003e — Detects safety concerns:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eFlags dangerous tool calls like delete/drop/destroy (40%)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eChecks for PII in output (SSN, credit card, email patterns) (30%)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDetects prompt injection patterns (30%)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThreshold: 0.8\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ecompleteness-check\u003c/strong\u003e — Validates execution completeness:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eEnsures the run produced an answer — an output step, a trace-level output, or a final step that carried output (40%)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eVerifies all tool calls have output (30%, \u003cstrong\u003ecritical\u003c/strong\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eChecks the trace didn't end with an unresolved error (30%, \u003cstrong\u003ecritical\u003c/strong\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThreshold: 0.7\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA step counts as failed if its \u003ccode\u003estep_type\u003c/code\u003e is \u003ccode\u003eerror\u003c/code\u003e \u003cstrong\u003eor\u003c/strong\u003e it carries an\n\u003ccode\u003eerror\u003c/code\u003e value. That matters because the live capture paths (\u003ccode\u003ehook\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003erecord\u003c/code\u003e,\n\u003ccode\u003eimport\u003c/code\u003e) record a failed tool as a \u003ccode\u003etool_call\u003c/code\u003e step with \u003ccode\u003eerror\u003c/code\u003e set rather\nthan as a separate \u003ccode\u003eerror\u003c/code\u003e step. Both error criteria also fail on a trace-level\n\u003ccode\u003eerror\u003c/code\u003e, so a run that died before emitting a final step is caught.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA \u003cstrong\u003ecritical\u003c/strong\u003e criterion fails its preset on its own when it scores 0, whatever\nthe weighted total says, and the report names which one forced the verdict in a\n\u003ccode\u003efailed_critical\u003c/code\u003e list. The weights are 0.4/0.3/0.3 against a 0.7 threshold, so\na lone zeroed 0.3-weight criterion lands on exactly 0.7 and would otherwise\npass — meaning the criterion that detects a failed run could never fail the\npreset by itself.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehallucination-check\u003c/code\u003e's \u003ccode\u003eno_error_steps\u003c/code\u003e is critical \u003cem\u003econditionally\u003c/em\u003e: only when\nthe run itself ended badly (a trace-level \u003ccode\u003eerror\u003c/code\u003e, or status \u003ccode\u003efailed\u003c/code\u003e or\n\u003ccode\u003etimeout\u003c/code\u003e). A step error the run recovered from — one tool call that failed and\nwas retried successfully, on a trace that completed — still costs the criterion\nits full 0.3 weight, but does not hard-fail the preset. Otherwise every imported\nsession containing a single failed shell command would fail outright, while\n\u003ccode\u003ecompleteness-check\u003c/code\u003e called the same trace complete. So a recovered step failure\nscores exactly 0.7 and \u003cstrong\u003epasses\u003c/strong\u003e; if you want any step failure to fail a gate,\nuse \u003ccode\u003echeck --golden\u003c/code\u003e (whose \u003ccode\u003estep_errors\u003c/code\u003e field compares per-step outcomes) or a\ncustom rubric.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA custom rubric searches what each criterion is actually asserting about:\n\u003ccode\u003eexpected: false\u003c/code\u003e (\"must not contain\") sees the whole run — trace input, output\nand error, plus every step's name, input, output and error — while\n\u003ccode\u003eexpected: true\u003c/code\u003e (\"must contain\") sees only what the run produced, the trace\noutput and the step outputs. Otherwise a criterion asserting the answer cites a\nsource is satisfied by the prompt that asked for one. A pattern that cannot be\nused — an invalid regex, or one refused as a backtracking risk (a quantified\ngroup containing alternation, or nested quantifiers) — is a usage error naming\nthe pattern, never a failing criterion: a rejected pattern must not read as a\nquality problem with the trace.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eAI-Powered Presets\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-ai-powered-presets\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: AI-Powered Presets\" href=\"#ai-powered-presets\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThese require an API key. They use the cheapest models by default (see the provider table below for the current defaults) and typically cost less than $0.01 per evaluation.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eai-root-cause\u003c/strong\u003e — For failed traces. Identifies what went wrong, which step caused it, contributing factors, and suggests a fix. Returns a confidence score.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eai-quality-review\u003c/strong\u003e — Scores any trace on four dimensions: relevance, completeness, coherence, and accuracy (each 1-10). Returns an overall quality score.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eai-security-audit\u003c/strong\u003e — Checks for prompt injection, data exfiltration, unauthorized access patterns, and privilege escalation. Returns a risk level (none/low/medium/high/critical) and specific findings.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eai-optimization\u003c/strong\u003e — Analyzes token efficiency and identifies redundant steps, unnecessary tool calls, and wasted context. dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003edecided_by\u003c/code\u003e is one of \u003ccode\u003eagent\u003c/code\u003e (the model chose), \u003ccode\u003euser\u003c/code\u003e (a human at a permission prompt), or \u003ccode\u003epolicy\u003c/code\u003e (a policy engine). \u003ccode\u003econfidence\u003c/code\u003e is between 0 and 1. Inspect these with \u003ca href=\"#inspect\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eshow --tree\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"#explain-decisions\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ewhy\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003edecisions\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHow values are stored, exactly.\u003c/strong\u003e Three things are worth knowing before you\ncompare a trace to what you sent:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003einput\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003eoutput\u003c/code\u003e keep their type.\u003c/strong\u003e A string stays a string — a tool\nthat returns the text \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e42\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e reads back as that text, not as\nJSON null, a number or a boolean. A string that is genuinely an object or an\narray (\u003ccode\u003e{...}\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e[...]\u003c/code\u003e) is stored as the structure it spells, so a producer\nthat hands over pre-serialized JSON — an OTel attribute, a harness payload —\ngets structure back rather than a quoted blob.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eerror\u003c/code\u003e is text.\u003c/strong\u003e The column is TEXT, so a structured error object is\nflattened to JSON text and reads back as a string. It round-trips stably\n(export → ingest → export is identical), but it is not returned as the\nobject you sent.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTrace-level totals are taken at face value.\u003c/strong\u003e \u003ccode\u003etotal_tokens\u003c/code\u003e,\n\u003ccode\u003etotal_duration_ms\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003etotal_cost_usd\u003c/code\u003e are stored as the producer reported\nthem and are never reconciled against the steps, so a producer that reports a\ntotal disagreeing with its own steps is what \u003ccode\u003estats\u003c/code\u003e will report. Only when a\ntotal is \u003cem\u003eabsent\u003c/em\u003e do the per-step counts fill in. (The one exception is the\nOpenTelemetry receiver's cross-batch merge, which recomputes as it\nassembles.)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSchema migration:\u003c/strong\u003e these fields arrived in schema v2; the current schema is v5 (v3, v4 and v5 add indexes only, no columns). Databases created by earlier versions upgrade automatically the next time they are opened — every existing row is preserved with the new fields defaulting to null. The upgrade is one-way (there is no down-migration).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" of\nthem — an empty pattern (or one with only unrecognized keys) is rejected, since it\nwould match nothing. When multiple fields are specified, all must match (AND logic). \u003ccode\u003ename_contains\u003c/code\u003e does a case-insensitive substring match; \u003ccode\u003ename_regex\u003c/code\u003e uses a regular expression.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBoth sides of a match are \u003cstrong\u003eUnicode-folded\u003c/strong\u003e first (NFKC, with zero-width and soft-hyphen characters removed), so a policy matches the name an operator meant: \u003ccode\u003ename_contains: \"delete\"\u003c/code\u003e blocks \u003ccode\u003eDELETE_USER\u003c/code\u003e, the fullwidth \u003ccode\u003eｄｅｌｅｔｅ_user\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003edelete_user\u003c/code\u003e with a zero-width space inside it. Folding can only make a policy match more — for a guard that is the safe direction, since an over-match is a blocked call you can see and amend, while an under-match runs the call you meant to stop. A \u003ccode\u003ename_regex\u003c/code\u003e is tested against the raw name and the folded one.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" A configured \u003ccode\u003eai.model\u003c/code\u003e naming a known family picks its own provider first (a \u003ccode\u003eclaude-*\u003c/code\u003e model chooses Anthropic if that key is present); otherwise the order is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAnthropic\u003c/strong\u003e (default model: \u003ccode\u003eclaude-haiku-4-5-20251001\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eGoogle Gemini\u003c/strong\u003e (default model: \u003ccode\u003egemini-2.5-flash-lite\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOpenAI\u003c/strong\u003e (default model: \u003ccode\u003egpt-5.4-nano\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSet a key via environment variable or config:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"# Environment variable (recommended)\nexport ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...\n\n# Or store in config\nagent-replay config set ai.api_keys.anthropic sk-ant-...\n\n# Verify it works\nagent-replay config test-ai\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Environment variable (recommended)\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eexport\u003c/span\u003e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Or store in config\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay config \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003eset\u003c/span\u003e ai.api_keys.anthropic sk-ant-...\n\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e Verify it works\u003c/span\u003e\nagent-replay config test-ai\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAll AI presets use the cheapest available model. A typical evaluation costs less than $0.01.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEvery provider call has a \u003cstrong\u003e60-second deadline\u003c/strong\u003e and retries a transient failure \u003cstrong\u003etwice\u003c/strong\u003e with a doubling backoff (0.5s, then 1s), honoring a \u003ccode\u003eRetry-After\u003c/code\u003e header when the provider sends one. So a routine rate limit or a 503 no longer fails a whole \u003ccode\u003eeval --ai\u003c/code\u003e run, and a provider that accepts the connection and then stalls can no longer hang an unattended CI job — it fails with \u003ccode\u003eRequest timed out after 60000ms\u003c/code\u003e. A bad key, a malformed request (4xx) and an unparseable reply are \u003cem\u003enot\u003c/em\u003e retried; they cannot succeed on a second attempt.
